item.title: $20m expansion
item.description: DULUX Paints Fiji, the manufacturers and distributors of paint products in Fiji and the Pacific, will be investing between $20-$25 million in a new manufacturing and production plant in Lami. The investment – fully funded by the company – will cover the acquisition of land, the demolition of current structures and the construction of the new facility.
item.content:encoded:
DULUX Paints Fiji, the manufacturers and distributors of paint products in Fiji and the Pacific, will be investing between $20-$25 million in a new manufacturing and production plant in Lami.

The investment – fully funded by the company – will cover the acquisition of land, the demolition of current structures and the construction of the new facility.

In an interview with this newspaper, Dulux Paints Fiji chief executive officer Roshan Singh said this plan was now progressing, and they had identified and acquired six different lots next to the current property at Nukuwatu.

“We are required to expand because our volumes are growing, the demand is growing, our product range is also growing,” Mr Singh said.

“So to meet the demand from our Fiji and Pacific markets, we need to have this investment.

“The current factory that was invested by our shareholders and directors 40 years ago, that took us this far. We want to invest into a facility that will take us 20 years forward, that will be able to meet the demands coming 20 years ahead.”

Mr Singh said the new facility will cater for manufacturing and production.

He said they planned to launch the new factory in the next two years.

“Our target is mid of 2028 and that’s what we’re working towards.”

Mr Singh said the multi-million dollar facility would be semi-automated, with the focus of introducing technology that reduced the human impact in the production.

“But the main focus of this factory is increasing our volume, increasing our production capacity and the main thing is making sure we are environmentally sustainable.

“We are looking at renewable energy and we are also looking at wastewater recycling.”

Mr Singh said they were also expecting challenges along the way and they had a team ready to counter those.

He said this new investment would mean customers in Fiji and the Pacific would have a world-class product that was manufactured in volumes and would be price competitive as well.

Dulux Paints sells 70 per cent of its products in country and the other 30 per cent is sold to the export markets.

It exports to Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Kiribati, Nauru and Wallis and Futuna.

item.title: BAT’s green push
item.description: THE British American Tobacco (BAT) company in Fiji is expected to save 60 per cent off its electricity bills after the installation of new solar energy systems to power its Nabua and Nadi facilities. BAT Fiji general manager James Goldring said the newly commissioned solar systems had cost an estimated $1.5million; and had a combined installed capacity of 806-kilowatt peak.
item.content:encoded:
THE British American Tobacco (BAT) company in Fiji is expected to save 60 per cent off its electricity bills after the installation of new solar energy systems to power its Nabua and Nadi facilities.

BAT Fiji general manager James Goldring said the newly commissioned solar systems had cost an estimated $1.5million; and had a combined installed capacity of 806-kilowatt peak.

“The system here at Nabua has an installed capacity of 660-kilowatt peak, while our system in Nadi has a capacity of 146 kilowatt peak,” Mr Goldring said.

He said the two systems were expected to generate 880 kilowatt hours of renewable solar energy annually and supply 60 per cent of BAT Fiji’s total electricity requirements.

“At the Nabua site, the solar installation is projected to reduce BAT Fiji’s carbon emissions by 32 per cent.

“By investing in renewable energy and energy efficiency, BAT Fiji is not only reducing our operational emissions but also helping to manage our reliance on the grid, particularly during peak times.”

Mr Goldring said the project was also contributing towards BAT Fiji’s sustainability targets of achieving 50 per cent renewable energy usage and reducing carbon emissions by 50 per cent by 2030, compared with 2020 levels.

“This installation forms part of BAT’s broader sustainability program aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions, managing climate-related risks and improving the use of energy and natural resources.”

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said the systems were expected to provide a significant share of BAT Fiji’s electricity requirements while substantially reducing emissions from its operations.

Mr Rabuka congratulated BAT Fiji for the investment and said the Government supported the continued operation and expansion of renewable energy initiatives.

item.title: Hardware firm doubles up
item.description: Hardware company Kasabias Pte Ltd has opened its second shop in the northern town of Labasa. Kasabias Pte Ltd national manager retail, marketing, information technology and customer service Nitinesh Chandra said the company had invested more than $1million into the establishment of the new outlet.
item.content:encoded:
Hardware company Kasabias Pte Ltd has opened its second shop in the northern town of Labasa.

Kasabias Pte Ltd national manager retail, marketing, information technology and customer service Nitinesh Chandra said the company had invested more than $1million into the establishment of the new outlet.

“This investment reflects on our ongoing commitment to the Northern Division, and includes infrastructure development, inventory expansion, operational resources, and staffing to better serve our growing customer base in the north,” Mr Chandra said in a statement.

“We invite everyone – from homeowners and DIY customers to builders, contractors and businesses to visit us, meet our team and allow us to be part of your next project,” he said.

The hardware shop’s new outlet is located on the main Naseakula Rd.

Tui Labasa Ratu Jone Qomate and company chairman Kasmukh Patel officiated at the opening on Thursday.

item.title: M-PAiSA up for award
item.description: DIGITAL Financial Services Pte Ltd (DFS) – the subsidiary of Vodafone Fiji that operates the mobile money platform M-PAiSA – has been named a finalist in the highly coveted PayTech of the Year category at the Asia Fintech Awards 2026. The Asia Fintech Awards recognises excellence, innovation, and impact among the region’s leading financial technology providers.
item.content:encoded:
DIGITAL Financial Services Pte Ltd (DFS) – the subsidiary of Vodafone Fiji that operates the mobile money platform M-PAiSA – has been named a finalist in the highly coveted PayTech of the Year category at the Asia Fintech Awards 2026.

The Asia Fintech Awards recognises excellence, innovation, and impact among the region’s leading financial technology providers.

DFS general manager Shailendra Prasad said being selected as a finalist was a significant achievement for Fiji and a testament to the impact M-PAiSA had made in transforming financial services across the country.

“It’s a proud moment for our team. The Asia Fintech Awards are highly competitive, attracting submissions from some of the most innovative and highly regarded fintech companies across the region,” Mr Prasad said in a statement.

“For M-PAiSA to be recognised as a finalist among such distinguished industry peers is both commendable and a tremendous honour.”

Mr Prasad said the nomination demonstrated that a home-grown Fijian digital wallet platform could successfully compete shoulder-to-shoulder with some of Asia’s largest and most sophisticated financial technology providers.

“It validates our vision, our investment in innovation, and our unwavering commitment to delivering accessible financial services to all Fijians.

“We are proud that our efforts to improve access to financial services and drive economic participation have been recognised on such a prominent and prestigious regional platform.”

The nomination also reflects the company’s ongoing efforts to expand the digital payments ecosystem in Fiji through innovative solutions that enabled customers to transact, save time, and participate more fully in the digital economy.

“We are honoured by this recognition and grateful to our customers, partners and stakeholders who have supported our journey.

“While being named a finalist is already a significant achievement, we remain hopeful of securing the ultimate award and bringing this prestigious recognition home to Fiji.”

The Asia Fintech Awards are among the region’s most respected industry awards, celebrating organisations that are driving innovation and redefining the future of financial services across Asia-Pacific.

The winners will be announced at a gala awards ceremony in Singapore on August 21.

item.title: Teen vows to fight drugs, urges unity
item.description: THE newly crowned Miss FMF Duavata Northern Crime Prevention princess 2026 is calling on the public to stand together in the fight against bluetoothing and substance abuse. Besila Drauna said the issue continued to threaten families, communities and the nation’s youth.
item.content:encoded:
THE newly crowned Miss FMF Duavata Northern Crime Prevention princess 2026 is calling on the public to stand together in the fight against bluetoothing and substance abuse.

Besila Drauna said the issue continued to threaten families, communities and the nation’s youth.

The 14-year-old of Naseakula Village, outside Labasa, made the plea after being crowned at Subrail Park on Friday night.

Miss Build More Designs PTE Ltd Amanda Robinson was named first runner-up.

Ms Drauna said her advocacy throughout the week-long carnival focused on raising awareness about the dangers of bluetoothing as children as young as her age were involved in cases of drug abuse.

“I hope that through my advocacy and that of the other contestants, we have inspired people to have open conversations, seek help when needed, and work together to protect the next generation,” she said.

She said she did not expect to win the crown as competition was tough.

“However, it has been a journey of growth, service, and advocacy. This win is dedicated to my support group at home, not forgetting my namesake who travelled from Taveuni to be present every night.

“Although only one person wears the crown, each one of the contestants is a winner. You have all inspired me with your courage, confidence, and passion for serving our community.”

She said she would continue to raise awareness about the dangers of bluetoothing and encourage young people to make positive choices for a brighter future.

item.title: ‘Retaining personnel a challenge’
item.description: retaining skilled personnel is the biggest challenge facing the Republic of Fiji Navy as trained personnel leave for better-paying opportunities, Navy Commander Timoci Natuva says. Commander Natuva said the navy was building new capabilities, but keeping the people needed to operate them remains a greater concern.
item.content:encoded:
retaining skilled personnel is the biggest challenge facing the Republic of Fiji Navy as trained personnel leave for better-paying opportunities, Navy Commander Timoci Natuva says.

Commander Natuva said the navy was building new capabilities, but keeping the people needed to operate them remains a greater concern.

“One of our big challenges now is sustaining our people, making sure that our people stay in the navy,” he said.

He said recruiting people was relatively easy, but retaining them was more difficult because of pay, allowances and opportunities available outside the navy.

“There are more opportunities out there in terms of the skill set that we have.”

“A lot have, in the last few years, some have resigned, left for greener pastures in Australia, New Zealand, US, some to other agencies in Fiji.”

Commander Natuva said the loss of trained and technically skilled personnel presents a significant challenge for the navy as it expands its operational capabilities.

“All the technology capability is good, but for us here the people is the priority.”

He said the navy was working to ensure personnel are properly looked after through pay, allowances and welfare support.

Commander Natuva said retaining the navy’s personnel would remain critical to ensuring the service could sustain the capabilities it’s building.

item.title: Graham Leung’s sacking as AG via Viber revealed in High Court ruling
item.description: Former Attorney-General Graham Leung was dismissed by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka through a Viber message while he was on a work trip in Hong Kong, details revealed in a High Court judgment show. The circumstances surrounding Leung’s termination on May 30, 2025, are outlined in Justice Dane Tuiqereqere’s ruling on judicial review challenges against findings of the Commission of Inquiry into the
item.content:encoded:
Former Attorney-General Graham Leung was dismissed by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka through a Viber message while he was on a work trip in Hong Kong, details revealed in a High Court judgment show.

The circumstances surrounding Leung’s termination on May 30, 2025, are outlined in Justice Dane Tuiqereqere’s ruling on judicial review challenges against findings of the Commission of Inquiry into the appointment of former FICAC Commissioner Barbara Malimali.

According to the judgment, Leung stated in a supplementary affidavit that he had messaged the Prime Minister several times during May 2025 regarding the anticipated COI report but received no response.

On May 30, Leung was in Hong Kong for work when he was woken in the early hours by a telephone call from the Cabinet Secretary informing him that he needed to speak urgently with the Prime Minister.

Leung then immediately sent Rabuka a message on Viber asking whether the Prime Minister wanted to speak with him.

According to the judgment, Rabuka responded by Viber “a minute later”.

“I am dismissing you as AG effective immediately under the provisions of the Constitution that empower me to,” the Prime Minister’s message stated.

“You may complete your trip there as there is nothing to sign on behalf of Fiji [in Hong Kong].”

The judgment states the Viber message was followed by a letter from the Prime Minister dated May 30, 2025.

In the letter, Leung was advised that “in light of the recommendations” of the COI report into Malimali’s appointment, the Prime Minister had decided to exercise his power to dismiss him as a minister with immediate effect.

Justice Tuiqereqere’s judgment elsewhere found that Leung had not been given notice of the adverse findings against him before his termination.

The court found that Leung would have been “blindsided” by the Commissioner’s adverse findings and was entitled, as a matter of natural justice and procedural fairness, to receive notice of the draft adverse findings and an opportunity to respond.

The High Court has since quashed the adverse findings and recommendations arising from the COI and declared the report null and void in its entirety.

item.title: Heavy rain alert issued for parts of Fiji
item.description: The Fiji Meteorological Service has issued a heavy rain alert for Viti Levu, Yasawa, Mamanuca, Kadavu and nearby smaller islands. The alert was issued at 9.10am today by the National Weather Forecasting Centre in Nadi.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Meteorological Service has issued a heavy rain alert for Viti Levu, Yasawa, Mamanuca, Kadavu and nearby smaller islands.

The alert was issued at 9.10am today by the National Weather Forecasting Centre in Nadi.

The weather service says an easterly wind flow is prevailing over Fiji, while a trough of low pressure approaching from the west is affecting the western parts of the country.

Residents in the affected areas can expect occasional rain, with isolated heavy falls and thunderstorms.

The Fiji Meteorological Service is advising people to remain alert, particularly in areas prone to flooding and other impacts from heavy rainfall.
